Winds of 39-61 kph or intermittent rains may be expected within 36 hours.

ROSAL MAINTAINS ITS STRENGTH WHILE OVER THE SEA EAST OF TAIWAN.

Location of eye/center : The center of the eye of Typhoon ROSAL was estimated based on all available data at  at 460 km North of Itbayat, Batanes (24.9, 122.4).
Strength : Maximum winds of 155 kph near the centerand gustiness of up to 190 kph.
Forecast movement : Forecast to move North Northwestward at 25 kph

Forecast position : 
Oct 24, 2026 08:00 AM - 525 km North of Itbayat, Batanes (OUTSIDE PAR)
Oct 24, 2026 08:00 PM - 725 km North of Itbayat, Batanes (OUTSIDE PAR)

HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
Severe Winds
 
The wind signals warn the public of the general wind threat over an area due to the tropical cyclone. Local winds may be slightly stronger/enhanced in coastal and upland/mountainous areas exposed to winds. Winds are less strong in areas sheltered from the prevailing wind direction.

Minimal to minor impacts from strong winds are possible within any of the areas under Wind Signal No. 1.

The periphery of ROSAL will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
 
Today (23 October): Most of Luzon and Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Misamis Occidental, Basilan, Tawi-Tawi, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental.
Tomorrow (24 October): Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Norte, Aurora, northern Quezon, Polillo Islands, Bicol Region, Romblon, Capiz, Iloilo, and Negros Occidental.
Sunday (25 October): Batanes and Babuyan Islands.

HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
A Gale Warning is in effect over the seaboards of Northern Luzon. For more details, refer to Gale Warning No. 7 issued at 5:00 PM today.

24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook 
Up to very rough or high seas over the following coastal waters:
Up to 8.0 m: The northern seaboard of Batanes.
Up to 6.0 m: The remaining seaboards of Batanes; the northern seaboard of Babuyan Islands.
Up to 5.0 m: The remaining seaboards of Babuyan Islands; the northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte; the northeastern seaboard of mainland Cagayan.
Up to 4.5 m: The remaining seaboards of Ilocos Norte and mainland Cagayan; the seaboard of northern Ilocos Sur.
Sea travel is risky for all types or tonnage of vessels. All mariners must remain in port or, if underway, seek shelter or safe harbor as soon as possible until winds and waves subside. 

Up to rough seas over the following coastal waters: 
Up to 4.0 m: The remaining seaboards of Ilocos Sur; the seaboard of northern La Union and Isabela; the northwestern seaboard of Pangasinan.
Up to 3.5 m: The seaboard of northern Aurora; the northern seaboards of Camarines Norte and Camarines Sur; the northern and eastern seaboards of Catanduanes and Northern Samar; the eastern seaboard of Eastern Samar.
Up to 3.0 m: The seaboard of Zambales; the remaining seaboards of Aurora; the northern and eastern seaboards of Polillo Islands; the eastern seaboards of Albay, Sorsogon, Dinagat Islands, Siargao-Bucas Grande Islands, and Surigao del Sur.
Mariners of small seacrafts, including all types of motorbancas, are advised not to venture out to sea under these conditions, especially if inexperienced of operating ill-equipped vessels.

Up to moderate to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
Up to 2.5 m: The western seaboards of Bataan and Lubang Islands; the remaining seaboards of La Union and Pangasinan; the eastern seaboard of Davao Oriental.
Up to 2.0 m: The western seaboards of Batangas, Cavite, Occidental Mindoro and Palawan including Calamian Islands; the remaining seaboards of Lubang Islands; the northern seaboard of Kalayaan Islands.
Mariners of motorbancas and similarly sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.

Other coastal waters have forecast wave heights of less than 2.0 m.

TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
It must be emphasized that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still be experienced in localities outside the landfall point and the forecast confidence cone. Refer to “Other Hazards affecting Land Areas” for more details. Furthermore, the track may still shift within the limit of the forecast confidence cone.
In the near term, ROSAL will make a counterclockwise loop while over the sea east of Taiwan. It will then move slowly northward and exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by tomorrow (24 October) morning. Afterwards, it will accelerate northward towards Japan.
ROSAL is forecast to gradually weaken in the next 12 hours. As it moves over the East China Sea, rapid weakening will begin and it may be downgraded into a severe tropical storm by tomorrow.
